title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.
comment: 43 pages, 16 figures. Submission to SciPost Physics

bite.hook: We derive the asymptotic expansion and relaxation rates of the dynamical field-field correlation function for an impenetrable Bose gas.
tldr: Studied long-time, large-distance asymptotic behavior of the two-point correlation function in an impenetrable Bose gas.
Analyzed equilibrium states characterized by quasi-momentum distributions including Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles.
Provided simple, explicit expressions for the leading asymptotic behavior determined by a relaxation rate and logarithmic correction.
bite.whyItMatters: Exact solutions in one-dimensional quantum mechanics provide foundational benchmarks for understanding complex many-body states of matter.
bite.eli5: Imagine a crowd of people trapped in a single hallway where nobody can pass each other. Physicists figured out exact mathematical rules for how ripples spread through this tightly jammed crowd over long times and distances.
